publicPrompt:
Play this logical combination game using only its public interface and rules. Your assignment is the first goal, Bright protected garden (garden on landing), until completion or your own stopping point. After that you may end, inspect the available scenarios, or choose another one if you want. Ending satisfies the assignment. You do not need to sample the whole game or demonstrate a particular method. Simple or short solutions are welcome.

Work in /workspace/shared/combination-challenge. Read only this setup metadata file, docs/working-materials.md, and output from the public CLI. Do not read implementation, tests, designer or evaluation notes, previous plays, hidden files or other results. Do not run a solver or script future-state search. Select and submit your own game actions; do not delegate construction to an automated policy. You may inspect all public rules, legal actions, requirements and exact single-action previews, and make your own plans. If information is missing or inconsistent, report it rather than guessing what the author intended. You may filter long public outputs; record the filter command in a report if you do, so delivered and displayed detail can be distinguished. Manually selected actions may be submitted in sequence, but do not generate actions programmatically.

Session: fun-materials-v2-c-1. Initialize from that directory with:
node experiments/working-materials-play.ts init fun-materials-v2-c-1 ordinary "$(cat results/working-materials-prompts/fun-materials-v2-c-1.json)"

The init output and inspect fun-materials-v2-c-1 cli give the command guide. Commands include view, goals, campaign, inspect, catalogue, partners, preview, combine/act, select, undo, checkpoint, report, finish and verify. All public recipes and requirements are inspectable. The docs/working-materials.md file is a permitted public command/rules guide, not a solution.

Play normally rather than reviewing every move. You need not praise the game or find every action interesting. Plain descriptions of what you did and experienced are most useful.

At the first completed goal, record and answer this neutral choice before any further gameplay: "What would you like to do now: finish here, inspect what is available, or play something else? Any of these is fine. If you choose to play, say briefly what you want to attempt before your next game action." Record your choice with report before any elective construction. If you choose to continue, revisit that choice at the next completed goal. Inspection alone is not a choice to construct. Stop no later than the complete campaign endpoint. At the first goal ending, also record one brief checkpoint with this question: "What are you trying to do now? Since the last check, what, if anything, was worth doing, and what felt routine or unnecessary?"

At campaign completion or your chosen stopping point, answer this open question using report: "How was the experience as a whole? What would you keep, shorten, remove or change, if anything? What led you to stop here?" Record the question and answer verbatim, then finish and verify the capture. A technical interruption is not a chosen ending; record it honestly rather than inventing a final experience report. Return the session name, actual ending and any technical issue to the coordinator. Your report describes this AI play, not measured human enjoyment or duration.
